name: Gemistocytic Astrocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Presence of gemistocytic astrocytes with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and eccentric nuclei on histological examination
MRI showing a diffusely infiltrative, often non-enhancing cerebral mass lesion typically in the cerebral hemispheres
IDH1 or IDH2 mutation status and ATRX loss supporting astrocytic lineage

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological identification of gemistocytic astrocytes combined with molecular markers consistent with astrocytoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other glioma subtypes and correlation with clinical and radiological findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits correlating with tumor location

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment including memory and executive dysfunction

searchTerms: loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: feeling sick from increased brain pressure

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to tumor mass effect
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific but may show mild protein elevation
Histopathology revealing gemistocytic astrocytes with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm
imaging: MRI showing diffusely infiltrative cerebral mass, often hypointense on T1 and hyperintense on T2/FLAIR sequences
Minimal or no contrast enhancement on MRI
Mass effect with possible midline shift in larger tumors
other: Elevated intracranial pressure signs in advanced cases
Slowly progressive clinical course compared to other astrocytomas

distinguishingFeatures: Different histopathological appearance with more fibrillary astrocytes
Presence of necrosis and microvascular proliferation on histology

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as persistent vomiting and papilledema
references: Louis DN, Perry A, Reifenberger G, et al. The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary. Neuro Oncol. 2021.
Kleihues P, Cavenee WK. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System. IARC; 2016.
